title: Universal Genève Polerouter – Tropical Dial
description: A Foundational Genta Design The Polerouter is the watch that launched the career of legendary designer Gérald Genta. Released in 1954, it was commissioned by Scandinavian Airlines to commemorate their pioneering flights over the North Pole, requiring a watch that could withstand the intense magnetic fields. Genta, then only 23, delivered a masterpiece of mid-century design with his signature twisted lugs and a clean, functional layout. It is one of the most important and accessible pieces from the mind that would later create the Royal Oak and Nautilus. The Beauty Of A Natural Color Shift This example is distinguished by its stunning tropical dial. The original black surface has aged over decades into a rich, varied brown, a natural process caused by long-term exposure to sunlight. This "tropicalization" is a unique and random occurrence that cannot be replicated, giving each watch its own specific character. The effect on this piece is particularly compelling, with different shades appearing depending on the light, all centered around a sharp crosshair pattern and accented by dauphine hands. It is paired with its original Universal Genève beads of rice bracelet. An Honest Vintage Timepiece The stainless steel case and dial are in great cosmetic, untouched condition. The dial's transformation from black to a deep, shifting brown is the main event. There is a scratch on the dial near the 9 o'clock position. The crown is a replacement, while all other parts are original to the watch. The original beads of rice bracelet is intact and fits up to a 7-inch wrist. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. Wearable History This Polerouter offers an uncommon combination of historical design significance and the unique aesthetic of a tropical dial. It is a watch for someone who appreciates the story behind a timepiece and the organic beauty that only time can create. The 35mm case with its elegant twisted lugs is perfectly sized for modern wear, offering a piece of Genta's legacy that is both a conversation starter and a reliable daily companion.

title: 1965 Rolex Oysterdate Precision 6694 – Silver Dial
description: A Pure Expression Of Rolex The Oysterdate Precision 6694 was a mainstay in the Rolex catalog for decades, acting as a gateway to the brand for a generation of owners. It pairs the legendary water-resistant Oyster case with a robust manual-wind movement, offering a pure, focused time-and-date experience. This reference represents the foundational principles of the company: durability, legibility, and timeless design, all in a watch that requires direct interaction from its owner. Clean Mid Century Character This example from 1965 captures the clean aesthetic of the era perfectly. The silver sunburst dial is versatile and classic, shifting its appearance depending on the light. The original luminous plots have developed an even patina over time, adding a layer of warmth and authentic vintage character that cannot be replicated. It is a simple, balanced design that has remained relevant for over half a century. An Honest And Original Example This watch presents in honest, original condition. The case, dial, crown, and movement are all original to the piece. The silver sunburst dial is well-preserved, and its aged lume is consistent with a watch from this period. It is fitted to a stainless steel Oyster bracelet. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. The Daily Ritual Of Winding This is the right choice for someone who wants to experience the core of vintage Rolex. The 34mm case is comfortable and understated, working in any situation without demanding attention. As a manual-wind watch, it offers a tangible connection that an automatic cannot. The daily ritual of winding the crown creates a bond between the owner and the machine, a small moment of focus that is increasingly rare. It is an ideal starting point for a new collector or a perfect daily watch for a seasoned one.

title: 1993 Rolex Datejust 16233 - Champagne Diamond Dial
description: A Balanced Luxury Classic The Rolex Datejust 16233 is the definitive execution of the world’s most recognizable luxury watch. While the steel and gold configuration is a staple, this example is elevated by the factory champagne dial set with diamond hour markers. The 16233 transitioned the model into the modern era with the introduction of the sapphire crystal and the caliber 3135 movement, offering a level of durability and precision that remains the industry benchmark. It is a watch that carries significant visual weight without feeling dated. A Cohesive Two Tone Aesthetic The combination of 18k yellow gold and stainless steel creates a high-contrast look that defines the Datejust’s legacy. This specific configuration with the diamond-set dial pushes the watch into a more formal category while retaining the versatility of the Jubilee bracelet. It is an all-matching example that feels complete, representing the era of Rolex manufacturing where build quality and luxury finishes met in a perfectly balanced 36mm case. Strong Case And Clean Components The case and 18k gold fluted bezel are in great shape, showing sharp lines and clear definition. The champagne dial is excellent, with the factory diamond settings remaining bright and secure. The two-tone Jubilee bracelet stretch appropriate for age, but is still in good shape overall and clearly unpolished. Mechanically, the watch is running strong after passing our test bench. The Ultimate Daily Statement This is a watch for someone who wants the most iconic version of the Datejust with an added layer of prestige. It works as well with a suit as it does in a casual setting, offering a level of recognition that few other timepieces can claim. It is a reliable, classic Rolex that feels substantial and looks exactly how a luxury watch should.

title: IWC - Blue Dial
description: A Study In Seventies Elegance International Watch Company built its reputation on robust, over-engineered tool watches, but their dress pieces from the 1970s show a different side of the brand. This manual wind watch captures the era's shift toward sleeker, more expressive design. The blue sunburst dial was a confident and less common choice for the typically conservative Schaffhausen manufacture, offering a vibrant alternative to the standard silver and white dials of the day. It is a piece that prioritizes clean lines and pure color. Integrated Form, Legendary Engineering The design is a masterclass in 1970s integration. The steel mesh bracelet flows directly from the case, creating a seamless, unified look on the wrist that was a hallmark of the period's style. Inside is the manual wind Caliber 403, a reliable and well-regarded workhorse movement from IWC's golden era. This combination of a minimalist dial, integrated form, and a legendary caliber makes for a complete and compelling vintage package. Untouched And Honest Condition The stainless steel case is in great cosmetic, untouched condition. The blue sunburst dial has a few small marks that are consistent with its age and visible in the photography. All components, including the crown, dial, and movement, are original to the watch. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. The Ritual Of The Daily Wind This is a perfect entry point into the world of vintage IWC for someone who values understated quality. The 34mm case wears beautifully as either a dedicated dress watch or a sophisticated casual piece. Winding the Caliber 403 each morning is a tactile ritual, a direct connection between the owner and the machine. It is a watch for someone who appreciates pure 70s design and the simple, enduring quality of a well-made movement.

title: Chopard St Moritz - White Dial
description: Here's a vintage Chopard Moritz in quartz with a white Roman numeral dial from the 1980s. Keeps great time and is fully functional. Recently serviced! Measurements include a 29x41mm square case size and 18mm lug width. Integrated bracelet with screws that fit up to a 7.5 inch wrist (butterfly clasp) Blue cabochon crown. White dial. Matching stick hands and hour markers. Quickset date function at 6 a clock. Nice polished finishing on both the case and bracelet. The bracelet and case shimmer, depending on the light. Drilled lug holes. 8 screws on the steel bezel. The bracelet has both a matte and polished finishing. Makes for a great watch for both men and women. A nice thin profile, makes for a great Cartier Santos alternative! All the parts are original including the crown, dial, movement, and caseback. Both the dial and case are in great cosmetic, untouched condition. Ready to wear!

title: Piaget 9151 – Blue Lapis Dial
description: An exquisite expression of 1970s haute horlogerie, this vintage Piaget reference 9151 is a rare and elegant timepiece that merges precious materials, bold design, and meticulous craftsmanship. Housed in a 25mm rectangular case crafted from solid 18k white gold, this ultra-slim, manually wound gem is paired with its original integrated white gold mesh bracelet — a hallmark of Piaget’s signature fusion of jewelry and timekeeping. The highlight is undoubtedly its deep blue lapis lazuli stone dial, punctuated with four brilliant-cut diamond markers and finished with white gold dauphine hands. Each lapis dial is unique, and this one is especially vibrant, with a rich mineral texture that subtly shifts in the light — a stunning contrast against the icy tone of the white gold. The case, bracelet, and dial are all in unpolished, untouched condition, and the original factory caseback sticker remains intact — a rare detail that speaks to the watch’s careful preservation over the decades. Mechanically, it’s fully functional and keeps excellent time, a testament to Piaget’s refined manual-wind movements of the era. All parts are 100% original, including the signed crown, dial, movement, and caseback. The integrated white gold mesh bracelet fits wrists up to 7.25 inches, draping like silk and giving the piece its unmistakably luxurious presence. This watch is more than just a rare vintage Piaget — it’s a wearable work of art, combining a lapis stone dial, diamond indices, and precious metal architecture in a way that remains utterly distinctive today. Perfect for collectors of stone-dial watches, Piaget aficionados, or anyone looking for a uniquely elegant vintage piece with real statement power. Now available exclusively through our New York City boutique or online. Don’t miss the chance to own this stunning and seldom-seen Piaget classic.

title: Hublot MDM Diver – Black Dial
description: The Original Hublot Vision Before the Big Bang, there was the MDM. This collection represents the original vision of founder Carlo Crocco, who introduced the radical concept of pairing a luxury case with a natural rubber strap in 1980. It was a move that challenged the conventions of Swiss watchmaking. This MDM Diver from the 1990s is a direct descendant of that philosophy, applying the "Art of Fusion" to a functional tool watch with 300 meters of water resistance. It is Hublot in its purest, most essential form. A Clean Expression Of 90s Design This example stands out for its clean, purposeful aesthetic. The 36mm steel case hits a sweet spot for modern wearability, offering a comfortable presence without the aggressive dimensions of later models. Its design is focused and legible, with a simple black dial featuring dot indices, bold luminous hands, and a quickset date at three o'clock. A functional rotating bezel completes the tool-watch functionality. This is a watch from an era when Hublot was more about a quietly confident design language than overt complexity. Untouched And Entirely Original The watch is in great cosmetic condition. The steel case and dial are both well-preserved and appear untouched, retaining their original finishes. All components, including the signed crown, dial, and movement, are original to the watch. The Hublot rubber strap remains in excellent shape. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. A Different Kind Of Hublot This is for the person who appreciates the history of Hublot but prefers the understated confidence of its early designs. The 36mm size and classic diver layout make it an incredibly versatile daily watch. It carries the weight and design heritage of a major brand while offering a look that stands apart from its contemporary catalog. It is a smart, functional piece of watchmaking history.

title: Franck Muller 7501 – White Arabic Dial
description: The Shape Of Independent Watchmaking The reference 7501 is a pure expression of what made Franck Muller one of the most important names in 1990s independent watchmaking. The Cintrée Curvex case was a technical and aesthetic statement, a rejection of the conservative round cases that dominated the industry. This design required curving the entire movement to follow the contour of the wrist, a challenge most brands avoided. This piece captures the brand's signature style from its most influential period, pairing the iconic tonneau shape with stylized Arabic numerals and a precious metal case. Classic Proportions In White Gold This example is a study in classic Muller design. The 18k white gold case provides a substantial but understated presence on the wrist. Its clean white dial, contrasted by elegant blued hands and expressive numerals, is the definitive look for the brand. The proportions are perfectly balanced, offering a distinctive shape without the oversized feel of some later models. A sub-seconds register at six o'clock adds a touch of traditional horological detail to the otherwise avant-garde design. Excellent Untouched Condition This piece is in great cosmetic, untouched condition. Both the 18k white gold case and the white dial are very well preserved. All parts are original to the watch, including the signed Franck Muller crown, dial, movement, and caseback. It is fitted to an aftermarket pink leather strap, which is secured by the original signed Franck Muller gold buckle. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. A Statement Of Design Literacy This is a watch for someone who appreciates the revival of mechanical watchmaking and wants a piece with a distinct point of view. The tonneau case is not just a shape, it is a marker of a specific, highly creative moment in modern watch history. It is comfortable, elegant, and immediately recognizable to those who know. This Franck Muller works because it makes a statement about taste and an understanding of craft, standing apart from more common choices.

title: Chopard St. Moritz – Two Tone White DIal
description: Refined sport-luxury, done right This vintage Chopard St. Moritz Automatic from the 1990s is a clean expression of the model at its most wearable. Executed in stainless steel and 18k yellow gold, it carries the unmistakable St. Moritz design language — integrated bracelet, sculpted case, and screw-accented bezel — in a configuration that feels both familiar and quietly elevated. Balanced, composed, and easy to live with. Why this configuration works The St. Moritz represents Chopard’s early take on refined sport-luxury, and two-tone automatic examples like this sit at the heart of the collection. The white dial keeps the watch crisp and versatile, while applied Roman numerals and a date window at six o’clock add just enough complication without cluttering the layout. The integrated steel and gold bracelet flows naturally into the case, reinforcing the sculptural design that made the St. Moritz feel ahead of its time when introduced — and still relevant today. It’s a configuration that highlights proportion and execution rather than excess, which is exactly why it wears so well decades later. Preserved as intended The watch presents in excellent, excellent condition, both cosmetically and mechanically. The case and bracelet remain well preserved, the dial is clean and evenly aged, and the overall presentation reflects careful ownership. Powered by its automatic movement, the watch is fully functional and keeps excellent time. All components are original, including the signed Chopard crown, original dial, movement, case, and caseback. A clean, confident St. Moritz This isn’t an experimental or overworked variation — it’s a strong, well-executed St. Moritz that does exactly what the model was meant to do. Elegant enough for formal settings, versatile enough for everyday wear, and distinctive without trying to stand apart. A solid vintage choice for many different reasons, and a reminder of why the St. Moritz remains one of Chopard’s most enduring designs.

title: Bvlgari Scuba SC38S – Black Dial
description: Italian Design Meets Swiss Engineering The Bvlgari Scuba represents a unique moment from the 1990s when the legendary Italian design house fully committed to producing serious, functional sports watches. Introduced as part of the Diagono collection, the Scuba blended the brand's signature bold aesthetic with the legitimate utility of a diver's chronograph. It was a confident move that set Bvlgari apart from traditional Swiss watchmakers, offering a piece that was as much a style object as it was a tool. The SC38S captures this ethos perfectly, with a design that is unmistakably Bvlgari. A Clean Example From The '90s This reference SC38S stands out as a well-preserved piece from its era. The 38mm case is a versatile size that wears comfortably today, bridging the gap between vintage proportions and modern presence. The black dial is clean and functional, equipped with a dual-subdial chronograph and a unidirectional rotating bezel for practical timekeeping. The use of a rugged rubber strap underscores its identity as a true sport-luxury watch, ready for any environment. Untouched And Well Preserved The watch is in great cosmetic condition. Both the steel case and black dial are untouched, showing honest integrity. The hands and hour markers have developed a matching patina, a detail collectors look for as a sign of originality. All components, including the signed Bvlgari crown and caseback, are original to the watch. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. A Confident Alternative This is the right choice for someone who appreciates high design and wants a distinctive alternative to mainstream divers. It carries the weight and heritage of one of the world's great jewelers, yet functions as a robust and capable sports watch. The Bvlgari Scuba is for the person who values brand identity and thoughtful design just as much as mechanical capability. It makes a strong statement without being loud.

title: Baume & Mercier Tank 37059B - 18K Yellow Gold Faux Tiger Eye Dial
description: The Seventies Evolution Of A Classic Form Baume & Mercier has long occupied an esteemed position within the horological landscape, celebrated for its ability to infuse classical Swiss watchmaking discipline with expressive, avant-garde styling. The 1970s marked a definitive era of experimentation for the house, moving away from traditional round configurations to embrace bold, geometric profiles. This "Tank" reference 37059B is a masterfully proportioned distillation of that design philosophy, utilizing a tailored 25x33mm rectangular silhouette. Executed in solid 18k yellow gold, the architecture delivers a sophisticated, low-profile alternative that carries a rich vintage presence on the wrist without relying on sheer scale to make an impact. The Warm Visual Depth Of The Exotic Dial The undeniable centerpiece of this rare timepiece is its stylized faux tiger's eye dial. During the 1970s, luxury houses confidently leaned into organic textures, using artistic mediums to capture the multi-tonal, horizontal striations of exotic stones. This dial presents a deep, warm canvas of gold and amber bands that play beautifully with incoming light, offering the immense depth of a mineral dial with excellent structural resilience. By completely eliminating standard hour markers, hands, and secondary text, the minimalist layout allows the rich texture of the dial to blend seamlessly with the surrounding 18k yellow gold case, treating the watch face as a pure piece of wearable art. Very Good Preservation And Slender Proportions Overall condition is very good. The solid 18k yellow gold case has been beautifully preserved, retaining its sharp rectangular transitions, uniform thickness, and clean lines. The caseback remains highly detailed, displaying a crisp, deep serial number stamp (658358) alongside its factory hallmarks. The faux tiger's eye dial is in immaculate condition, showing no signs of fading, moisture ingress, or environmental breakdown. Fitted to a premium leather strap, the watch wraps fluidly around the anatomy of the wrist. Mechanically, the manual-wind movement has been thoroughly bench-tested and verified, confirming strong performance and excellent operational reliability. An Understated Touch Of Retro Luxury The reference 37059B is a timepiece built for the individual who values historical design execution and quiet connoisseurship. Powered by a thin, manual-wind caliber, it fosters a direct, physical connection between the owner and the mechanical soul of the watch through the daily ritual of winding. Its compact 25x33mm dimensions ensure an incredibly comfortable fit that sits entirely flush against the skin, slipping effortlessly under any formal dress sleeve. Clean, honest, and increasingly difficult to source in this tier of preservation, it remains an elegant and character-rich statement piece of independent vintage luxury. Key Specs Reference: 37059B Model: Tank Era: 1970s Movement: Manual Wind Case Size: 25x33mm Bezel: 18K Yellow Gold

title: Cartier Baignoire Allongee - Sapphire Diamond Pave
description: This ultra-rare neo-vintage Cartier Baignoire Allongée is a masterpiece of elegance, rarity, and design innovation—an extraordinary reference that transcends traditional watchmaking and flirts with high jewelry territory. Crafted in solid 18k white gold and powered by a mechanical hand-wound movement, this piece dates to the early 2000s and represents one of the most elusive and exquisite versions of Cartier’s beloved “bathtub” silhouette. The standout feature here is, without question, its factory-set sapphire dial . While most Baignoire Allongée watches feature traditional Roman numeral dials, this example showcases two tones of expertly cut natural blue sapphires arranged in a seamless, radiant mosaic. The depth, color variation, and vibrancy of the stones shift beautifully in the light, making this one of the most unique dials ever produced by Cartier. Only a handful of these sapphire-dial variants are known to exist, placing this reference among the rarest Cartier creations ever offered to the public. Its signature elongated oval case—measuring a graceful 22mm by 47mm—sits elegantly on the wrist, with its curvature allowing it to conform comfortably to nearly any wrist size. This example comes complete with an original Cartier navy blue strap and matching 18k white gold deployant clasp, a pairing that perfectly complements the deep tones of the dial while remaining classically understated. This watch has been recently serviced and is running flawlessly. It is in great and honest condition, with all parts 100% original, including the dial, case, and movement. The case retains its crisp definition, and the dial remains untouched and immaculate. This Baignoire Allongée isn’t just a rare Cartier—it’s a celebration of what makes the maison so revered: elegance, restraint, craftsmanship, and daring beauty. Whether you're a seasoned Cartier collector or someone looking to own a uniquely significant timepiece, this sapphire-dial Allongée is a trophy-level acquisition. Offered watch-only, as is common with these early 2000s pieces, and now available exclusively through our flagship New York City boutique or online. Don’t miss this once-in-a-lifetime example.

title: Audemars Piguet – Two-Tone Zebra
description: Discover a truly exceptional timepiece: the Audemars Piguet “Zebra,” an ultra-rare vintage watch that stands as a testament to the brand’s bold design language and mechanical mastery. Nicknamed for its distinctive two-tone vertical stripe pattern that runs seamlessly across the case and integrated bracelet, the “Zebra” is unlike anything else on the market—a captivating blend of avant-garde aesthetics and timeless Swiss craftsmanship. This watch is not just rare; it's virtually mythical. Very few examples have ever surfaced, making it a dream acquisition for collectors who understand the value of exclusivity. Every detail of the Zebra speaks to a bygone era of daring design and meticulous engineering. The mechanical movement inside beats with the soul of traditional horology—no batteries, no shortcuts—just pure mechanical artistry. Featuring screw links for easy and precise sizing, the integrated bracelet doesn't just follow your wrist—it becomes part of it. Every stripe, every link, every turn of the crown reminds you that you’re wearing a piece of watchmaking history. This isn’t just a watch—it’s a conversation starter, a rare artifact, and a bold statement all in one. For those who value individuality, legacy, and the thrill of finding what few others ever will, the Zebra is an unrivaled treasure. title: Baume & Mercier – Blue Falcon Eye
description: A striking representation of 1970s luxury watchmaking, this vintage Baume & Mercier timepiece is crafted entirely in solid 18K yellow gold and features a rare and captivating blue Falcon’s Eye stone dial. Measuring 33mm across and fitted with an elegant integrated bracelet, this time-only manual wind piece showcases a perfect blend of refined case architecture and gemstone artistry. The dial is the star of the show: Falcon’s Eye, also known as Blue Tiger’s Eye, is a natural variety of quartz known for its shimmering chatoyancy and deep, silky blue hue with subtle streaks of grey and silver. While Tiger’s Eye—with its warm golden tones—is more commonly seen in vintage watch dials, Falcon’s Eye is significantly rarer, especially in factory-set examples like this. Its cooler, stormy aesthetic offers a more understated, moody elegance, making it highly sought-after among collectors of hardstone dials. Complementing the dial are sharp Dauphine hands and a matching blue cabochon-set crown, enhancing the cohesion and detail of the design. The integrated bracelet, also in 18K yellow gold, flows seamlessly from the case and gives the watch a sculptural, jewelry-like presence. The piece weighs a substantial 63.4 grams, emphasizing its quality and solid construction. Inside beats a manual wind movement, fully functional and keeping excellent time. All components—the case, dial, and movement—are 100% original and in excellent vintage condition, reflecting Baume & Mercier’s understated yet luxurious approach to watchmaking during this period. This is a truly rare and elegant example from the golden era of stone dial watches, ideal for collectors who appreciate natural materials, vintage craftsmanship, and the quiet power of distinctive design. Bracelet extending or cutting is available by request! SKU - 752

title: Cartier Tonneau - 18K Rose Gold
description: This elegant neo-vintage Cartier Tonneau Ref. 2850K in 18K rose gold captures the refined spirit of Cartier’s design language from the 1990s — a period celebrated for its timeless shapes and understated luxury. The silver guilloché dial, adorned with black Roman numerals and blued Breguet-style hands, reflects the maison’s mastery of proportion and detail. Its tonneau-shaped case wears beautifully on the wrist — slender, balanced, and unisex in its appeal. The caseback is clearly numbered with an early serial of 231, and the watch retains all the original components, including the case, dial, and manual-wind movement. This particular example is presented in mint condition, fitted with a burgundy bespoke alligator strap that perfectly complements the warmth of the rose gold case, secured by its original 18K rose gold deployant clasp. A subtle yet striking combination that enhances the watch’s timeless elegance. Pure in form and uncompromising in craftsmanship, this Tonneau embodies the essence of Cartier’s golden design era — an exquisite choice for the collector who appreciates enduring style, rarity, and refinement.

title: Chopard Onyx - Integrated Laykin & Co Stamped Retailer Signature Dial
description: A Masterclass In Eighties Opulence The 1970s and 80s were a playground for Chopard, a period where they moved away from traditional watchmaking constraints to focus on high-concept jewelry pieces that happened to tell time. This Ref. 2036 1 is a heavy hitter from that era. It features a deep, bottomless onyx dial housed in a yellow gold case, but the real draw is the "Retailer Signature" with Laykin & Co. Retailer stamps like this are historical fingerprints; Laykin & Co. was the premier luxury destination at the Fairmont Hotel in Los Angeles, catering to the Hollywood elite. Seeing their name alongside Chopard on a dial like this anchors the watch to a very specific, high-society West Coast history . Bamboo Gold And Deep Onyx The design language here is unapologetically bold. The integrated 14K yellow gold bracelet is finished in a "bamboo" style, a texture that was incredibly popular for high-end jewelry-watches during this period because of how it catches the light without looking like a standard flat link. The contrast between the organic, textured gold and the stark, sterile black of the onyx dial creates a balance that feels sophisticated rather than loud. It is a configuration that captures the exact energy of 1980s luxury . Condition And Reality The watch is in good, honest condition. The 18K yellow gold case and bezel have maintained their definition, and the integrated bracelet remains structurally sound with a total weight of nearly 100 grams, giving it a significant, high-quality presence on the wrist. The onyx dial is clean, showing no cracks or chips which is the primary concern with stone dials from this era. Mechanically, the movement is running strong after passing our test bench . Why It Works This is a piece for the collector who wants something that feels like an artifact. It sits in that perfect pocket of being a serious horological item due to the Chopard pedigree and Laykin & Co. stamp, while functioning primarily as a piece of sculptural jewelry. It works because it doesn't try to be an everyday tool; it is a specialized, era-defining statement that remains wearable today because of its refined proportions and classic color palette. It’s a distinct choice for someone who values provenance and style in equal measure .

title: Concord Year of Dragon - Enamel Dial
description: The 1-of-50 Enamel Dragon The Concord "Year of the Dragon" is a legitimate sleeper in the world of high-art horology. Produced in a strictly limited run of 50 pieces in 1998, this is an artifact of traditional craftsmanship that typically commands six-figure entries from the "Holy Trinity" houses. It features a genuine, hand-painted enamel dial—a material prized for its eternal color and depth. This isn't a mass-produced print; it is a microscopic work of art that represents a rare moment where Concord leaned into high-end artisanal execution. Hand-Painted Artistry The dial depicts a fierce, intricate dragon motif rendered in vivid enamel and accented by diamond hour markers. Enamel dials are notoriously difficult to produce, as the repeated firing process often results in cracks that ruin the entire piece. Finding a perfectly preserved example is a rarity. The 18k gold case measures 25mm x 34mm, offering a refined, rectangular silhouette that allows the artistry of the dial to be the undisputed focal point. It manages to feel both symbolic and sophisticated, providing a level of detail rarely encountered outside of bespoke commissions. Condition and Performance Verified The piece is in overall excellent vintage condition. The 18k gold case and sapphire crystal are in excellent condition, ensuring the enamel work remains protected and clearly visible. It is a healthy, verified, and exceptionally rare opportunity to own a high-level enamel dial timepiece at an accessible entry point. It represents a specific, "if you know, you know" trophy for the collector who values technical craftsmanship over brand hype. Mechanical Integrity and Provenance Unlike many decorative pieces of the era, this Limited Edition houses a manual-wind mechanical movement visible through a clear exhibition caseback. It remains fitted to its original black alligator strap and matching 18k gold buckle, preserving the original factory aesthetic. This example is especially notable for its completeness, as it is accompanied by the original papers—a critical detail for a piece with a worldwide production run of only 50 units. title: 1995 Rolex Cellini 4084 - 18K White Gold
description: Undercover Gold TV Case The Rolex Cellini 4084 is a masterclass in mid-century inspired minimalism. This reference abandons the traditional round case in favor of a softened rectangular silhouette that feels both vintage and contemporary. While Rolex is defined by its tool watches, the Cellini line exists to showcase the brand's ability to handle precious metals and delicate proportions. The silver sunburst dial is the perfect anchor for this design, catching the light in a linear fashion that complements the clean 18k white gold case. A Study In Proportional Balance At 30x28mm, this is a watch that relies on its shape rather than its size to make an impression. The integrated lug design allows the leather strap to flow directly from the case, creating a seamless look on the wrist. Because it utilizes a manual-wind movement, the profile remains incredibly thin, ensuring it sits flat and unobtrusive. It is a configuration for the collector who appreciates the technical restraint required to make a watch this simple and this effective. Excellent Case Definition And Original Hardware The 18k white gold case is in great shape, showing sharp, well-defined edges and no significant softening of its unique geometry. The silver sunburst dial is equally well-preserved, remaining clear and free of any oxidation or spotting. This example is fitted to a leather strap and retains its original Rolex 18k white gold buckle, a critical component for maintaining the watch's integrity as a complete set. Mechanically, the movement is running strong after passing our test bench and provides a smooth tactile winding experience. The Understated Choice For Formality This is a watch for the person who wants the prestige of a Rolex without the bulk of an Oyster case. It is a refined, quiet piece of horology that prioritizes texture and form over utility. Whether worn as a dedicated dress watch or a sophisticated daily alternative, it offers a level of mid-century elegance that is increasingly difficult to find in modern catalogs. It is a timeless execution of the dress watch genre.

title: Cartier Santos Galbée - Two Tone Ivory Dial
description: The Contoured Two-Tone Classic The Santos Galbée Reference 187901 is the definitive 1990s evolution of Cartier’s most iconic silhouette. While the original 1904 design was a pioneer, the Galbée (French for "curved") update brought a necessary ergonomic flow to the square case, allowing it to hug the wrist properly. This execution in two-tone stainless steel and 18k yellow gold is the exact aesthetic that defined luxury for a generation, balancing industrial hardware with a high-jewelry finish that remains a staple of the Cartier catalog today. The Warmth of Ivory The centerpiece of this reference is the ivory Roman dial, which offers a softer, more vintage-leaning depth than the stark clinical white versions. This creamy tone provides a sophisticated bridge between the 18k yellow gold bezel and the stainless steel case. The dial layout is perfectly balanced with signature blued-steel sword hands and a railway minute track, anchored by a symmetrical quickset date window at the 6 o'clock position. It is a timeless configuration that prioritizes legibility while leaning into a richer, more classic color palette. Condition and Integrity This 187901 is an honest, untouched survivor that remains in great cosmetic shape. The ivory dial and sapphire crystal are remarkably clean, showing none of the spotting or "foxing" that can occasionally plague vintage Cartier stone or painted dials.
